questions.question: A dealer marks an article 40% above the cost price and gives two successive discounts of 20% and 25% on the marked price. If he suffers a loss of ₹140, then the cost price (in ₹) of the article is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Run the chain. 
MP = 140   ⇒  140 × 0.8 × 0.75 = ₹84 
 Step 2   That is a loss of 16 per 100. 
loss 16% = ₹140   ∴  CP = 140/16 × 100 = ₹875

questions.question: On an article marked ₹1600, successive discounts of y% and z% were given. As a result the item was sold for ₹1056. Which of the following options CANNOT be a set of values of y and z? ₹1600
questions.solution:
Step 1   What fraction of the marked price 
survives. 
1,056 / 1,600 = 0.66   ⇒  combined discount = 
34% 
 Step 2   Test each pair against y + z − yz/100 = 34. 
(a) 20, 17.5 → 34 ✓     (c) 4, 31.25 → 34 ✓     (d) 12, 
25 → 34 ✓ 
 Step 3   The odd one out. 
(b) 22, 15.5 → 37.5 − 3.41 = 34.09 ✗   — so (b) 
cannot occur

questions.question: The marked prices of a pen and pencil are in the ratio of 5:6. The shopkeeper gives an 18% discount on the pen. If the total discount on both the pen and pencil is 12%, then the discount offered on the pencil is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take the marked prices as 500 and 600. 
pen's discount = 18% of 500 = ₹90 
 Step 2   Total discount is 12% of both. 
12% of 1,100 = ₹132   ⇒  pencil's share = 132 − 90 
= ₹42 
 Step 3   As a percentage of the pencil's marked 
price. 
42 / 600 = 7%

questions.question: A dealer gives a discount of 7% on the marked price and gives 1 article free on every 25 articles purchased, and thus earns a profit of 25%. Find the percentage increase in marked price over the cost price (up to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Step 1   Selling 26 for the price of 25, at 7% off. 
SP = MP × (25/26) × (93/100) 
 Step 2   That selling price is a 25% profit, so with 
CP = 100: 
MP × (25/26) × 0.93 = 125   ⇒  MP = 26 × 500 / 93 
= 139.78 
 Step 3   Increase over cost. 
139.78 − 100 = 39.78%

questions.question: A retailer marked a jacket 60% above its cost price. During off-season clearance, he offered a flat discount of ₹1800 and still made a profit of 20%. What was the cost price of the jacket?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write the selling price two ways. 
MP = 1.6x   and   SP = 1.6x − 1,800 = 1.2x 
 Step 2   Solve. 
0.4x = 1,800   ∴  x = ₹4,500

questions.question: Rohan sells a bed by giving a 65% discount on its list price. If instead he had given only a 62% discount, the selling price would have been ₹6,000 more. What is the original marked price of the bed?
questions.solution:
Step 1   The gap between the two offers. 
65% − 62% = 3% of MP = ₹6,000 
 Step 2   Scale up. 
1% = 2,000   ∴  MP = ₹2,00,000

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows 16% discount on every item and still makes a profit of 8%. If he gives 8% discount instead of 16% on an item marked for ₹1800, what will be his profit percent
questions.solution:
Step 1   The 16% offer. 
SP = 1,800 × 0.84 = 1,512, which is 8% profit   ∴  
CP = ₹1,400 
 Step 2   The 8% offer. 
SP = 1,800 × 0.92 = ₹1,656   ⇒  profit = ₹256 
 Step 3   As a percentage of cost. 
256 / 1,400 × 100 = 18.29%

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 60% above its cost price (CP = ₹750). It is sold for ₹710.40, after two successive discounts of 20% and x%. If a single discount of 1.5x% is given on the same marked price, the loss percentage will be:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Marked price, then the first discount. 
MP = 750 × 1.6 = 1,200   ⇒  1,200 × 0.8 = ₹960 
 Step 2   960 falls to 710.40, which fixes x. 
710.40 / 960 = 0.74   ∴  x = 26 
 Step 3   Now the single discount of 1.5x = 39%. 
SP = 1,200 × 0.61 = ₹732   ⇒  loss = 750 − 732 = 
₹18 
 Step 4   As a percentage of cost. 
18 / 750 × 100 = 2.4%

questions.question: (HW) An item undergoes two successive discounts: 12.5% and then 20%. After those discounts, a tax of 18% is applied on the reduced price, and the final amount the customer pays is ₹927. What was the original price of the item?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write the whole chain as factors. 
P × 0.875 × 0.80 × 1.18 = 927 
 Step 2   Collapse and divide. 
P × 0.826 = 927   ∴  P = ₹1,122.28

questions.question: To clear stock, a seller gives an 8% discount on the marked price. He spends ₹x on promotion. Total cost of items is ₹2,50,000 and the marked price is 10% more than cost. He earns no profit or loss. What is the value of x? ː
questions.solution:
Step 1   Marked price, then the discount. 
MP = 2,50,000 × 1.10 = 2,75,000   ⇒  SP = 
2,75,000 × 0.92 = ₹2,53,000 
 Step 2   Set it against everything he spent. 
2,53,000 = 2,50,000 + x   ∴  x = ₹3,000

questions.question: A trader gives 5% discount on the marked price of an article and gives 4 articles free for buying 14 articles and gains 33% in the entire transaction. The marked price of an article is what per cent more than its cost price?
questions.solution:
Step 1   He is paid for 14 but parts with 18. 
SP / MP = (14/18) × (19/20) = 133/180 
 Step 2   The 33% gain fixes the third term. 
MP : SP : CP = 180 : 133 : 100 
 Step 3   Marked price against cost. 
(180 − 100)/100 = 80%

questions.question: Ramanna purchased raw materials to manufacture a product. 22.5% of the raw materials got wasted. 80% of the cost of raw materials used was added as manufacturing cost. Ramanna sells the product to earn an overall profit of 20% after offering a discount of 20%. How many times of total raw material cost was the marked price?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take the raw material as ₹1,00,000. 
22.5% wasted   ⇒  material used = ₹77,500 
 Step 2   Manufacturing is 80% of what was used. 
0.80 × 77,500 = ₹62,000   ⇒  total cost = 
₹1,62,000 
 Step 3   20% profit, then work back through the 
20% discount. 
SP = 1,62,000 × 1.2 = 1,94,400   ⇒  MP = 1,94,400 
/ 0.8 = ₹2,43,000 
 Step 4   Against the raw material cost. 
2,43,000 / 1,00,000 = 2.43 times

questions.question: (HW) A shopkeeper was offering two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on an item whose marked price is ₹1,000 while another shopkeeper was offering a flat 33% discount on the same item. Find the positive difference in the nominal amounts of discounts given by the two shopkeepers on the sale of the item.
questions.solution:
Step 1   The successive pair. 
1,000 × 0.8 × 0.85 = ₹680   ⇒  discount = ₹320 
 Step 2   The flat offer. 
1,000 × 0.67 = ₹670   ⇒  discount = ₹330 
 Step 3   Difference. 
330 − 320 = ₹10

questions.question: ₹3,600 is divided in such a way that half of the first part, one-third of the second part and one-fifth of the third part are equal. What is the value of the third part? ₹3,600
questions.solution:
Step 1   Read the ratio straight off. 
x/2 = y/3 = z/5   ⇒   x : y : z = 2 : 3 : 5 
 Step 2   Value one part. 
10 parts = ₹3,600 ⇒ 1 part = ₹360   ∴  third part 
= 5 × 360 = ₹1,800

questions.question: Sunderlal distributed his savings of ₹1,62,000 among his wife, 3 sons and a daughter in such a way that his wife gets double of what his daughter gets and his daughter gets double of what each of his sons get. How much will his daughter get?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Build the shares upward. 
son = 1   ⇒  daughter = 2   ⇒  wife = 4 
 Step 2   Total the parts. 
4 + 2 + (3 × 1) = 9 parts = ₹1,62,000   ⇒  1 part = 
₹18,000 
 Step 3   The daughter holds 2 parts. 
2 × 18,000 = ₹36,000

questions.question: According to the will of Ks, ₹21,25,000 was to be divided between the son and the daughter in the ratio 7/6 : 5/3. How much did the son get (in Rs.)? Ks
questions.solution:
Step 1   Put both over 6. 
7/6 : 5/3 = 7/6 : 10/6 = 7 : 10 
 Step 2   Value a part and take the son's 7. 
17 parts = ₹21,25,000 ⇒ 1 part = ₹1,25,000   ∴  
son = 7 × 1,25,000 = ₹8,75,000
